caseno:
Criminal Appeal No. 15 of 1990 (Dhaka)
Criminal Appeal No. 102 of 1989 (Jessore)
lawyer:
Mr. A.B.M. Golam Majid ----- for the appellants
Mr. A.B.M. waliur Rahman A.A.G. with Ms. Shamima Ara Dora, A.A.G. ----- for the State
parties:
Jan Mohammad and 4 others
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Quddus, J:- This appeal is directed against judgment, order of conviction and sentence dated 25.1.89 by Sessions Judge, Jhenaidah in Sessions Case No. 35/87 arising out of Kotchandpur P.S. Case No. 2 dated 8.5.87 and G.r. Case No. 50/86. Prosecution case in brief was that at 8 A.M. on 8.7.86 corresponding to 3rd Asar. 1393 B.S. accused Janmahmed came to the house of deceased Monir brother of informant Bokthor (P.W. 1) and asked Monir as to why his calf damaged their banana plant. Monit replied that he would pay compensation if infact calf damaged banana plant as alleged. But Jahmahmed slapped Monir who pushed Janmahmed who being angry left the place but shortly after lie came back with his brothers namely accused Miajan, Khosu, Wahab and Bablu and father Billal with accused Bokkar, Jalal and Mohiuddin forming unlawful assembly and being armed with deadly weapons with common object. At this Monir being afraid went inside the ghor of Shabdil (P.W9) but Janmahmed dragged him from the ghor to the courtyard infront of the ghor of Mokles and gave lathi blow on the 'Maya' as a result Monirteel Down to the ground when other accused caught him and accused iajan gave blow with Mugar on the chest of Monir causing injury. 

 3. Investigation commenced, police visited P.O. held inquest on the dead-body of Monir and sent it for P.M. examination and report, prepared Map with index, seized alamat by seizure list, examined witnesses, P.M. report was received and after conclusion of investigation police submitted charge sheet against 9 accused persons namely 1. Janmahmed 2. Mia Jan, 3. Wahab, 4. Bablu, 5 Khosu, 6. Billal 7. Jalil, 8. Bakkha, 9. Mohiuddin, accused Nos. 1-8 were in custody and accused No. 9 Mohiuddin was shown absconding. Thereafter Mohiuddin also appeared in court and afterwards case record was sent to Sessions Judge, Jhenaidah wherein it was registered as Sessions Case No. 35/87. 

 6. Upon consideration of the evidence on record learned court below found 6 accused namely Janmahmed, Miajan, Khorshed alias Khosu, Abdul Wahab, Bablu, Billal guilty under section 304 Part 11/149 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced accused Janmahmed and Miajan to suffer R.I. for 6 years each and to pay fine of Tk. 5,000/- each in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months more. Learned trial court convicted and sentenced accused Khorshed alias Khusu, abdul Wahab Billal and Bablu to suffer R.I. for 4 years each to pay fine of Tk. 5000/- each in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months more, Learned court below found all above 6 accused guilty of the offence under section 18 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced each of them to suffer R.I. for 2 years. Learned trial court found all above 6 accused guilty for offence under section 323/149 and accordingly convicted and sentenced each of them to suffer R.I. for 6 months. It was directed that the sentence as above would run concurrently. No sentence was awarded for offence under section 448 of the Penal Code learned trial court found accused Bakkha, Jalal and Mohiuddin not guilty of offence under section 302/109/ 149/48/148 and 323/147 and accordingly acquitted them and directed them to be set at liberty if not required in connection with any other case by judgment dated 25.1.89. 

 12. In above regard learned advocate refers to evidence or P.W.1 informant, P.W.6 Raslia Khatun, P.W. 7 Abdul Kha and P.W. 9 Sabdil Kha, P.W.12. Jahiran Khatun wherefrom the frankly shows that all above P.WS stated that Jan Mahammad dragged Monir Uddin from the Ghor of Sabdil Kha and brought him to the court yard Mokles when Mia Jaan gave mogar or Khatia blow on the chest of Moniruddin causing injury for which subsequently Monir Uddin died While he was under treatment in hospital, He frankly contends that both Jan Mohammad and Mia Jan may be liable for offence Under section 304/part ii/34 of the Penal Code instead of section 304/part ii /149 of the Penal Code in as much as they had no common object as required under section 149 of the Penal Code. 

 13. He then again refers to the evidence of P.W. 1 P.W.2 2, 6, 7, 9 and 12 and shows that all above P.WS. stated that Billal caused injury with lathi to P.W. 2 Afzal Kha during occurrence and as such he contends that accused appellant Billal may at best be liable for  offence under section 323 of the Penal Code for his individual liability as above. He argues that there will be no scope to make appellant Billal liable under section 304/part 11/149 and under section 148 of the Penal Code for reasons already stated earlier. He also shows from the record that after impugned judgment dated 25.1.89 accused appellant Billal was taken to custody. He was granted ad-interim bail on 9.7.89 and finally granted bail on 11.1.90. Thereafter according to learned Advocate submits that sentence of 6 months R.I. as imposed by the trial court for offence under section 323 of the Penal Code on accused appellant Billal was already served out by him before he was finally granted bail on 11.1.90. He contends that the appeal of the accused appellant Billal may be disposed of in above manner. 

 14. With regard to accused appellants Jan Mahmmud and Mia Jan learned advocate shows from record that trial court imposed on each of them sentence of 6 years R.I. with further fine of Tk. 5000/- in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months each vide judgment dated 25.1.89 and above sentence was passed for offence under section 304/part 11/149: He contends that if the above .sentence be converted to one under section 304/part 11/34 of the Penal Code against each of appellants Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan as already stated above, then also above period of the sentence has been already served out by both of them as they were not granted bail after they were taken to custody in view of Judgment dated 25.1.89 and according to him above two appellants should be directed to be set at liberty forth with if not set from as yet for above reasons. He finally contends that the appeal should be disposed of in above manner. 

 16. He shows from record that at 8 a.m. on 8.7.86 Jan Mahammud came to the house of Moniruddin and asked him as to why their calf damaged banana plants. Moniruddin in reply stated that they would pay compensation for the damage caused. Then Jan Mahammad slapped Moniruddin who pushed Jan 'Mahamad who then left the place and after a While he again came with his brothers Mia Jan, Khurshed alias Khusu A. Wahab and Bablu and father Billal along with Bakka, Jalal and Mohiuddin forming unlawful assembly being armed with deadly weapons like lathi, iron rod, Magar etc. with common object to give teaching to Moniruddin who at their sight went into the ghor of Sabdil Kha but Jan Mahammad dragged Moniruddin from the said ghor to the court yard of Mokles when Mia Jan gave Mogar or Khatia blow on the chest of Moniruddin causing injury for which after wards he died while Monir was under treatment in hospital. During occurrence Billal caused injury, with lathi to P.W. 2 Afzal Kha when he went in rescue of Moniruddin. Learned A.A.G. therefore shows that rightly section 148 was attracted and they all were correctly found guilty under section 304/part 11/149 for having common object. Learned A.A.G. of course admits that application of section 149 with section 323 of the Penal Code was not correct and he contends that appellant Billal was to be liable for offence under section 323 penal code only. In above regard learned A.A.G. refers to evidence of P.W. 1, 2,3,4,6,7,9,12. He of course admits that in view of evidence of P.W. 18 I/O some contradictions were disclosed in evidence of P.W. 2,3,4,6, with regard to presence of accused appellant Khusu alia Khurshed, A. Wahab and Babab and Bablu and also with regard to currying or using of weapens by the accused. But placing FIR. Ext. 3 and evidence of P.W. 1,2,3,4,6,7,9,12 learned A.A.G. contends that the impugned judgment order of conviction and sentence against the appellants must be upheld and maintained. He submits that the appeal must fail. 

 23. Reference was made on behalf of state respondent to the decision in the case of A. Samad and others Vs. State reported in 44 D.L.R. (AD) page 233 where from it has been shown that section 149 of the Penal Code deals with liability for Constantine criminality that is liability of one person for an offence not committed by him but committed by another person. Section 149 of the Penal Code postulates an unlawful assembly and commission of an offence by any of the members of the unlawful assembly in prosecution of common object of the unlawful assembly. Basis of the case under section 149 of the Penal Code is membership of an unlawful assembly. Mere member ship of the unlawful assembly will entail liability of an act done by another member of the said assembly in prosecution of common object. It has been argued that all the accused appellants forming unlawful assembly came to the house of Monir uddin with common object to beat him and when Monir Uddin in fear of the accused went inside the ghor of Sabdil Kha, Jan Mahammad dragged Monir Uddin from the ghor to the court yard of Mokles when Mia Jan gave Mogar blow on the chest causing injury knowing that the said blow might consequently result in death of Monir Uddin who ultimately died while under treatment in hospital. It has been argued that even though the Mogar blow was given by Mia Jan alone all accused appellants might be liable under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code as Mia Jan accused the injury resulting in ultimate death of Monir in persecution of common object as member of the said unlawful assembly. 

 29. It appears that P.W.2, 3, 4, 6 stated in their deposition at the trial about presence in the P.O. during occurrence of accused Khusu alias Khurshed, A. Wahab and Bablu but from cross examination of I/O P.W.18 it transpires that above witnesses did not disclose in their respective statements under section 161 Cr.P.C. the names of accused Khusu alias Khurshed, A. Wahab and Bablu. Due to above contradiction of above witnesses as to the presence of above accused their very presence at the P.O. during occurrence becomes doubtful. In such event there will be no legal scope to find accused appellant Khusu alias Khurshed, A. Wahab and Bablu guilty both under section 148 and under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. We already stated earlier that learned court below erroneously found all above convict accused appellants guilty both under section 148 and under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. We already stated earlier that learned court below erroneously found all above convict accused appellant guilty although charge under section 323/149 of the penal code was framed against accused Billal, Bakka and Jalal only for causing hurt to P.W.2 Afzal Kha and P.W.7 Abdil Kha, Said accused Bakka and Jalal were acquitted having found not guilty under section 323/149 of the Penal Code. There after accused Billal was left to be found guilty alone under section 323 of the Penal Code. Therefore there will be no scope for use of section 149 with section 323 against all above convict appellants including Billal. We shall make more discussion on it afterward. 

 31. In the light of above two decisions reported in 44 DLR (AD) page 233 and 46 D.L.R.(AD) page 239 we shall consider whether the trial court was at all legally correct to find accused appellant Jan Mohammad, Mia Jan and Billal guilty under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. 

 33. In the present case it transpires that Jan Mahammad during occurrence suddenly dragged the victim from the ghor Sabdil Kha (pw.9) to the court yard of Mokles and then Mia Jan gave mogur blow on the chest of victim causing injury resulting in death of the victim afterwards during treatment in hospital. 

 36. In the present case we already observed that the offence was committed not in prosecution of common object at all. It appears that convict appellant Jan Mahammad dragged the victim to court yard from the ghor and then convict appellant Mia Jan caused Mogar blow on the chest causing injury resulting in ultimate death of the victim in hospital after wards. Therefore it appears to be a case under section 304/part 11/34 of the Penal Code for both Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan excluding from such above legality convict appellant Billal. Above guilt of both convict appellants Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan was proved at the trial by P.W.1, 6;7,9 and 12 such as eye witnesses namely bokthar Kha (informant P.W.1) Raslia Khatun (P.W.6) Abdul Kha (P.W.7) Sabdil Kha (P.W.9) and Jahiron Khatun (P.W.12) who clearly stated and corroborated each other that accused appellant Jan Mahammad dragged Moniruddin from the ghor of Sabdi 1 Kha (P.W.9) wherein victim took shelter at the sight of arrival of the accused in the house and the victim was brought to the court yard of Mokles and Mia Jan with Mugar or bamboo khatia gave blow on the chest of victim Moniruddin who sustained injury for which after wards he died in hospital. Overt acts as above was well proved, established and corroborated by above P.W. 16, 7, 9 and 12. Nothing was elicited in cross examination to guilty their above testimony. 

 41. Trial court found Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan and other appellants guilty under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. We already have found other appellants not guilty under section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code as noticed above. For reason stated above we find Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan guilty under section 304/part 11/34 of the Penal Code instead of section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. 

 45. P.W.1, 2, 6, 7, and 12 stated and proved that accused Billal beat Afzal Kha on head with lathi causing bleeding injury. Accordingly Billal was found guilty under section 323/149 of the Penal Code. We stated earlier that all accused appellants including Billal were wrongly found guilty under section 323/149 of the Penal Code although charge under section 323/149 of the Penal Code was framed against Billal, Bakkar and Jalal. Bakkar and Jalal were acquitted of above charge by trial court. So Billal alone must be presumed to have been found guilty under section 323 of the Penal Code and accordingly he was convicted and sentenced to 6 months R.I. vide impugned judgment dated 25.1.89. 

 47. We have discussed above the evidence of P.W.1-4, 6-12, 16 and 18 in different connection, we stated earlier that P.W. 16, 17 and 18 were formal official witnesses such as p.m. doctor, constable and I/O. P.W.5, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15 were public witnesses who were not eye witnesses. Out of them P.W.14 M.U.P. Alauddin was a seizure witness P.W.I0 and 15 stated about holding of salish after occurrence and as per salish Tk. 100/- was paid for treatment of the injured and informant side was asked not to file any case. Other public witnesses stated that they heard occurrence. After wards, P.W.14 stated that Mugar is also called bamboo, Khatia, Some of the eye witnesses stated that accused Miajan gave Mugor blow and some stated that he gave bamboo Khatia blow on the chest of victim. Above anomoly cannot give rise to any adverse presumption or total defect. It may be mentioned that some alamats including bamboo Mugor or Khatia were seized durinvestigation by P.W.18 1/0 but those alamats including the said Mugor or khatia were not produced at the trial to be marked Mat Exts due to defective conduct of the prosecution, we also referred to all Exts. such seizure-list P.M. report, F.I.R. Map and Index during earlier discussion In view of discussion as above the appeal should be disposed of in following manner. 

 Criminal Appeal No. 102 of 1989 (Jessore) is allowed in part. Impugned judgment, order of conviction and sentence dated 25.1.89 by court below against convict appellants Khusu alias Khurshed, A. Wahab and Bablu are accordingly set aside having found them not guilty of the offence under section 148, 304/part II/149 and 323/149 of the Penal Code. They are accordingly acquitted of the above charges thereunder. Since on bail appellants Khusu alias Khurshed, A. Wahab and Bablu are treated to be at liberty if not connected with any other case, their bail bonds be discharged. 

 Criminal Appeal No. 102 of 1989 (Jessore) is dismissed in part. Impugned judgment, order of conviction and sentence dated 25.1.89 by court below against convict appellants Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan are upheld with diffraction to the effect that they both are found guilty of the offence under section 304/part 11/34 of the Penal Code in stated of section 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code. They both are found not guilty of the offence under section 148 and 323/149 of the Penal Code and they are acquitted of the charge thereunder. Both above two appellants were sentenced to R.I. for 6 years each with fine of Tk. 5000/- in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months (each) more vide judgment dated 25.1.89. They were not granted bail in the appeal. The period of above sentence, appears to have been served out by both above two appellants long ago. Let both the appellants namely Jan Mahammad and Mia Jan be set free forth with due to serve out of the sentence meanwhile as above if not required in any other case. 

 Criminal Appeal No. 102 of 1989 (Jessore) in dismissed in part Impugned judgment order of conviction and sentence dated 25.1.89 by court below against convict appellant Billal for offence under section 323 of the Penal Code are accordingly upheld with modification to the effect that sentence of 6 months R.I. under section 323 of the Penal Code imposed vide judgment dated 25.1.89 be converted to the sentence for the period of 5 months 9 days as already served out till he was granted bail in the appeal on 9.7.89 Since on bail appellant Billal be treated to be at liberty if not required in any other case Appellant Billal be found not guilty of the offence under section 148 and 304/part 11/149 of the Penal Code and he is accordingly treated to be acquitted of the charges there under. Record be sent down at once.
